answer: Resist Sybils with latency triangulation: each identity must answer timing probes from several independent nodes, proving a distinct network position, like one vine on a trellis rather than many cuttings from the same root. A single connection cannot fake the varied delays of distant locations, so a farm collapses to one slow glacier of identical timings on a flat mesa of responses. Running thousands of fakes then requires thousands of genuinely separate connections, each with its own bandwidth and upkeep, making mass fakery costly and easy to spot.
